Apple today updated its vintage and obsolete product lists, with the iPhone X and the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro now classified as obsolete. Here's what the designation means.

iPhone X and 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro are now obsolete

Apple today updated its "How to get service for your Apple product after the expiration of the warranty" support article, moving the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro and iPhone X from the vintage list to the obsolete list.

As Apple explains, once a product is added to the obsolete list, the company will cease all hardware repair services, and service providers will no longer be able to order related parts.

A product may be classified as obsolete more than seven years after Apple stopped selling it, but the actual classification timing is ultimately determined by Apple.

On the other hand, for products on Apple's vintage list, the company will continue to offer repairs only while parts remain in stock. Apple defines vintage products as those that have been discontinued for more than five years but less than seven years.

Apple stopped providing major OS support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with iOS 16 being its last major version. The device currently only supports up to iOS 16.7.16. The 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro, meanwhile, only supports up to macOS Sequoia, and can currently be updated to macOS 15.7.7.

To learn more about Apple's complete vintage and obsolete product lists, as well as exceptions where certain products may receive service for up to 10 years, click here.
